Cross-border ANOVA and response structure

Current revised grid · scenarios, regional setups and external closures

What is compared

The current results tag is 20261012_c79. Twelve interventions (HH-Food, HH-Energy, HH-Wood, Gov-Plastics, Int-Wood, Int-Pulp, Int-Plastics, Int-Metal, Int-Glass, Int-Cement, Int-Energy, Int-Food; presentation numbers sc1–sc12, D-51) are crossed with two regional setups, EU/RoW and North/South, and four external closures: gold, fiat, expenditure-adjusting OPENFIXG and quasi-float. Each intervention is measured against its own arm’s baseline, as the mean over t = 79..100, one cycle of the baseline accelerator (D-65). Inv-Construction, Inv-Metal, Int-Construction and Inv-Recycling, and the OPENFLEX diagnostic, are excluded.

The analysis retains signed responses in both regions across activity, fiscal, external, distributional, financial and ecological outcome blocks. Coordinates are standardized, and the six outcome blocks are weighted equally. A share below is a share of weighted response variation across this declared finite grid, rather than a causal contribution to one trajectory.

Readable scenario and observation codes

Use channel–material–closure–setup: for example, HH-Food-OPENFIX-gold-NS or Int-Metal-OPENFIXG-EU-RoW. HH means household consumption, Gov government consumption, Inv firm investment, and Int intermediate production. NS is North/South; EU-RoW is EU/rest of world. Gold and fiat remain explicit because OPENFIX alone would be ambiguous. HH and Int are alternative intervention channels; the material name identifies the substitution.

The submitted paper’s material-first abbreviations remain aliases; no simulation IDs or experiments are changed.

Variables and response units

The pooled analysis studies 37 variables in each region: 74 coordinates. A scenario profile keeps the eight configurations separately, giving 592 possible coordinates; 578 remain after dropping constant/nonfinite coordinates. Both representations standardize coordinates and give the six outcome blocks equal weight. Correlated and accounting-related coordinates are retained, so these are not 74 independent economic mechanisms.

Block Variables
Real activity Real activity Total Real Consumption (c); Value Added (va); Gross Output (go); Real Investment in Fixed Capital (id); Nominal Output (y); Final Demand in Real Terms (fd)
Fiscal Fiscal Government Deficit (gdef); Tax Payments (t); Government Spending (g); Government Debt (b_s); Debt to GDP Ratio (debt_gdp)
External External Real Final Imports (imp); Real Final Exports (rex); Current Account Balance (cab); Trade Balance (tb)
Labour and distribution Labour and distribution Employment (n); Female Employment (nf); Profit Share of Disposable Income (shp); Wage Share of Disposable Income (shw); Wage Bill (wb); Disposable Income (yd); Worker Disposable Income (ydw); Capitalist Disposable Income (ydc); Worker/capitalist income gap |1 - ydw/ydc| (rises when workers gain) (ineq)
Finance and wealth Finance and wealth Household Demand for Personal Loans (lh); Corporate Demand for Bank Loans (lf); Net Household Wealth (v); Fixed Capital Stock (k); Corporate Profit (f_f)
Ecological Ecological Production of Material Goods (x_mat); Land Used (land); Extraction of Matter (mat); Recycled Matter (rec); Annual CO2 Emissions (emis); Waste (wa); Water Used (water); CO2 Concentration (co2_cum)

Most measurements are percentage changes from the matching baseline. Current account, trade balance and government deficit are level differences divided by the region’s baseline value added, multiplied by 100. Wage/profit shares and debt/GDP use percentage-point differences; functional inequality uses 100 times its index difference. co2_cum is the catalogue’s CO₂-concentration stock measure, distinct from annual emissions. Employment and female employment measure labour demand; wage/profit income shares and class disposable incomes measure functional distribution rather than a household income-distribution Gini.

Factorial decomposition

For each response coordinate, the complete factorial model separates scenario, setup and closure effects and all their interactions:

\[ \begin{aligned}y_{sac}=\mu&+S_s+A_a+C_c\\&+(SA)_{sa}+(SC)_{sc}\\&+(AC)_{ac}+(SAC)_{sac}.\end{aligned} \]

The full 12 × 2 × 4 grid has 96 observations and 95 non-intercept degrees of freedom. There are no residual degrees of freedom. These ANOVA sums of squares are descriptive; they do not provide inferential F-tests or p-values.

term df weighted_sum_of_squares share_percent
scenario 11 344.614195 60.458631
setup 1 8.773433 1.539199
closure 3 2.285001 0.400877
scenario:setup 11 103.365680 18.134330
scenario:closure 33 45.087693 7.910121
setup:closure 3 3.142624 0.551337
scenario:setup:closure 33 62.731374 11.005504

Scenario differences account for 60.46% of weighted variation. Scenario × setup accounts for 18.13%, scenario × closure for 7.91%, and the three-way interaction for 11.01%. Small standalone setup and closure shares do not imply that these dimensions are unimportant: their effects depend substantially on the intervention.

Response grouping and sensitivity

Clustering groups observations by the geometry of their signed response vectors. It does not identify separate economic mechanisms. The selected number of groups changes with the permitted search range and minimum group size:

The pooled 4-group cut is selected over k=2…8. Wider searches or excluding singleton groups select different cuts. Scenario-profile grouping keeps the eight setup/closure configurations in separate coordinates. Search ranges, features, linkage and accounting correlations qualify the interpretation of all groups.

Change the group count to explore nested splits; highlight CD or a named intervention without removing surrounding branches.

Select a named leaf or regime tile to inspect it. Highlighting preserves the full hierarchy.

Reading this tree

Cut by cut

Each cut is a merge of the tree read from the root down: cut j takes the tree from j to j + 1 groups. Cuts that the current “Groups” setting has made are in full colour, deeper ones are greyed. Regime counts are the value-added rule’s tiles on each side (one per setup × closure configuration). “What separates them” lists the four responses whose standardised means differ most between the two sides, with each side’s median raw response averaged over t = 79..100 (one cycle) over its scenarios and configurations.

    How well supported is this cut?

    Method

    Tree. Rows are the leaves (scenarios, or individual observations); columns are their responses averaged over t = 79..100, each standardised over the rows and divided by the square root of the number of columns in its outcome block, so the six blocks (real activity, fiscal, external, labour and distribution, finance and wealth, ecological) weigh equally. The tree is agglomerative: it starts with every leaf alone and, at each step, merges the two groups whose union increases the total within-group sum of squared distances the least (Ward’s criterion, in the “D2” form that works on Euclidean distances). The merge height is that increase on the distance scale, so a long vertical gap before a merge means the two groups it joins are far apart. Cutting the tree at a height gives the groups; “cut j” in the reading above is the j-th merge counted from the root. The per-cut drivers are descriptive: per zone × variable, the mean over its columns of the difference between the two sides’ standardised means (R/scenarios/tree_split_drivers.R); they name what differs most, and are not the tree’s own weighting.

    Branch geometry uses Ward D2 on the standardised, equally block-weighted responses. Coloured circles identify statistical groups at the chosen cut. Regime tiles use the separate value-added rule; hover or focus them for signed responses.

    Regional setup. “EU/RoW only” and “North/South only” rebuild the tree on that setup’s responses alone, with the columns re-standardised over its rows; they are not slices of the both-setups tree. Distance. The standard distance mixes how hard a scenario moves the economy with which way. “Direction from the cross-scenario mean” rescales each standardised row to unit length, so only the angle between rows counts; because the columns are centred, it measures direction relative to the average scenario, and a nearly inert scenario (Sc6 Inv-Metal) points in the direction “opposite to the average”. “Direction from zero” divides each column by its root mean square without centring before rescaling rows, so it compares sign patterns relative to no response; Sc6 Inv-Metal’s direction is then numerical noise (responses of order 10⁻⁶ %).

    Left: each bar spans the range of Ward merge heights over which the tree has exactly k groups; a cut is robust when its bar is long and fragile when it is short. Right: mean silhouette by k. A leaf’s silhouette is (b − a)/max(a, b), where a is its mean distance to its own group and b to the nearest other group; it runs from −1 (closer to another group) to +1, and a leaf alone in its group scores 0 by convention. Kaufman and Rousseeuw read a mean of 0.26–0.50 as weak structure and 0.51–0.70 as reasonable. The per-leaf silhouette is drawn beside each leaf in the tree above.

    Why Int-Metal is active while Inv-Metal is nearly inert. Int-Metal (Mtl-Int) changes intermediate input composition. Inv-Metal (Mtl-FD) changes firms’ investment composition. Under revised investment equation R9, that composition weights net investment; replacement purchases follow the capital matrix. Near a stationary baseline net investment is almost zero, so Inv-Metal’s revised response is tiny. This does not establish that substituting replacement-capital purchases would be ineffective. The intervention has not been redefined here.

    PCA: the main response directions

    Principal component analysis (PCA) finds orthogonal directions capturing the most variation in the same standardized, equally block-weighted response space. It is a projection of response geometry, not an identified causal decomposition. Cluster colours below use the selected Ward cut; changing the cut does not change the PCA axes.

    For pooled observations, PC1 and PC2 together capture 66.09% and the first three 77.65%. For scenario profiles, the first two capture 80.13%. A two-dimensional plot therefore omits part of the distance used for clustering.

    Which variables define the axes?

    The largest absolute pooled loadings on PC1 concern region-1 real exports, region-2 real imports and region-2 loans, wealth, tax and corporate profits. PC2 emphasizes region-1 wealth, tax, value added, profits, corporate loans and imports. PC3 emphasizes public debt/deficit and trade-balance contrasts. These are statistical associations in weighted coordinates. Z1/Z2 are regional roles: EU/RoW in one setup, North/South in the other. The sign of a PCA axis is arbitrary.

    Two SC branches in the classification rule

    The fitted sign/threshold rule has two SC branches. The weak-response branch is evaluated first: the absolute partner-region VA response is below τ = 0.003% of its baseline. The other branch requires both regions to contract after the weak-response case has been excluded. These are rule branches, not independently discovered statistical clusters. On this grid their counts are 42 and 6.

    Rule branch Observations
    CD: Z1 expands, Z2 contracts 8
    FIC: energy, Z1 expands, Z2 contracts 11
    PL: Z1 contracts, Z2 expands 27
    SC: both regions contract 6
    SC: weak Z2 response 42
    UN: both regions expand 2

    Closure-by-scenario regime map

    CC (contained contraction) means a weak region-2 VA response; DC (dual contraction) means both regions contract beyond the weak-response branch. PL = production leakage, CD = competitive displacement (including the inherited fossil-import-collapse label), and DE = dual expansion. These D-61 labels are derived from the same value-added responses as the original classification. Each tile is a separate baseline-matched experiment.

    The heatmap shows each closure’s classification against its own baseline. Against gold, OPENFIXG changes 8 of the 24 broad labels across the two setups. The figure also shows branch changes within SC; identical broad labels can conceal different response magnitudes.

    What changes from the submitted paper?

    There are two comparisons using the inherited submitted classification codes. In EU/RoW under gold, 2 of 11 comparable scenarios differ from the submitted reference. Across the full revised grid, 25 of 88 comparable observations differ. sc12 Int-Food has no submitted reference, so its eight runs are excluded from that comparison. This is not a set of 88 matched old-model reruns.

    Signed transmission labels

    The inherited classification on 20261012_c79 applies the fixed threshold τ = 0.003% of region-2 baseline value added. Its SC code contains both the weak-response and both-contracting branches; the D-61 display maps these to CC and DC, maps FIC into CD, and maps UN into DE. The displayed five labels are descriptive response categories.

    Label Observations
    CD 8
    FIC 11
    PL 27
    SC 48
    UN 2

    The 96 current labels are classified on the high-finance, windowed grid. Numerical magnitudes and their decomposition come from the current tag. The quasi-float EU baseline retains the documented debt-slope exception, so acceptance of these observations is not a strict-stationarity or attraction claim.

    Sources and related analyses

    Current tables are read from transmission_structure_<tag>/ and transmission_regime_grid_<tag>/, selected by data/current_results.json. The calculations are implemented in R/scenarios/transmission_cluster_structure.R and R/scenarios/classify_transmission_grid.R.

    The Analysis section also retains the submitted-scenario cross-border ANOVA, its construction-excluded variant, and the dated pre-recalibration revised-grid analysis. Those are separate experiments. Documentation contains the calibration comparison and diagnostic reports; Discussion explains what the current evidence supports and what remains an author decision.
